title: The Live Extraction
premise: Wren Amberdale, a disgraced intelligence analyst living off the grid in Lisbon, receives a calendar invite from his handler—dead for six weeks—summoning him to a safehouse meeting. There he finds a stolen dossier proving a joint covert program has been disappearing refugees for organ and identity harvesting, and the only witness is the assassin sent to silence everyone who knows. Forced into an uneasy alliance with the killer, Nadia, whose sister was one of the disappeared, Wren must smuggle the evidence through three governments' dragnets to a journalist's extraction flight at dawn. They make the flight at terrible cost—Nadia stays behind as decoy and is captured—but her sacrifice forces the program's exposure, and Wren finally chooses belonging over invisibility by testifying publicly under his own name.
about_author: Casper Almeida is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent a decade inside institutions he can no longer discuss. He writes thrillers about people the system discards, from a farmhouse outside Porto.

chapters.title: Invitation from the Dead
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Six weeks after handler Elias Voss's funeral, Wren gets a calendar invite from Voss's account for 9 p.m. at a decommissioned tram depot. Paranoid but unable to resist, he goes, finding a dead courier, a burned laptop, and a single encrypted drive labeled with his old case number—the one that got him fired. Emotional beat: dread curdling into the addictive pull of purpose he thought he'd lost.

chapters.title: The Third Government
chapters.summary: Wren decrypts the drive: proof of 'Sable Harvest,' a trilateral program vanishing displaced people off European books. Before he can move, an assassin corners him in his flat—then lowers her gun when she sees the files. Nadia reveals she was sent to kill Voss's network; her sister was Sable Harvest victim forty-one. Emotional beat: enemies recognizing each other as the only allies left.

chapters.title: Nine Hours to Dawn
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren and Nadia POV. A night-long gauntlet: they bluff past a police checkpoint using Wren's old credentials, discover a mole inside the journalist's network, and realize all three governments are converging on the airfield. Wren nearly bolts to save himself; Nadia's quiet certainty about her sister shames him into staying. Emotional beat: found family forged under fire.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the airfield, the mole springs a trap; Nadia draws them off so Wren can reach the plane, and is taken. On board, Wren transmits everything—not anonymously this time, but signed with his real name. Weeks later, Sable Harvest collapses, and Wren begins searching for where Nadia is held. Emotional beat: grief transformed into resolve; invisibility traded for belonging.
